theme: Getting agents the right context, then paying less for it

articles.title: Context Engineering (Agent Memory) for AI Agents Starts with Retrieval
articles.focus: Read the Key Takeaways, then the sections on inefficient searching and too much context at once.
articles.summary: Agents have a limited context window, so retrieval can fail in three ways: inefficient searching, too much context at once, and irrelevant or stale context. The post works through a competitive analysis agent to show how the Deep Agents harness handles each failure.
insights: Search before you read: glob matches file names, grep finds matching lines without loading files into context, and read_file reads a page at a time.
Grep only matches exact text, so a query for 'Company A funding' misses 'Company A closes $50M Series B'. A retrieval tool backed by a vector store adds search by meaning.
Agentic retrieval lets the agent decide when and what to search while it works. The post contrasts this with 2-step RAG, which searches once and then answers.
For custom search tools, the post recommends 'retrieve, offload, delegate': save results to files, return the paths, and let subagents read them.
articles.career_fit: This extends your RAG homework from one-shot retrieval to agentic retrieval. Early-career agent roles such as LangChain's Deployed Engineer posting ask for exactly this kind of practical agent design.
articles.check_question: Why does an agent's filesystem search use grep before read_file?
articles.check_answer: grep finds matching text without loading whole files into the context window, so the agent spends context only on the parts that matter.

articles.title: From Intent to Improvement: Agentic Dataset Search for Better Model Training
articles.focus: Read the abstract, the three challenges in the introduction, and the conclusion. Skip the experiment details for now.
articles.summary: AgenticDS is a framework for finding training data, where a query mixes a semantic goal with hard constraints such as task, license, and training stage. Each model decision fills in a typed object before deterministic code uses it, and evidence is verified before a ranking is accepted.
insights: Text retrieval cannot enforce hard constraints. Free-form tool-calling agents add flexibility, but the same model that picks a dataset also declares it a match.
On the HuDS-Bench benchmark of 200 queries, AgenticDS improved NDCG@10 by 25.7% over the strongest dense-sparse hybrid and by 18.9% over a commercial LLM agent.
Relevance is not the same as training utility. A search-to-train study judged results by the accuracy of the model they trained, not by ranking scores alone.
The authors name two limits: the benchmark shares a graph with the retrieval engine, and the utility study is narrow in coverage.
articles.career_fit: NDCG is a core recommender metric from your course, so this connects ranking evaluation to agent design. The typed-contract pattern is also a concrete answer to interview questions about making agents reliable.
articles.check_question: What problem do typed contracts solve that a free-form tool-calling agent leaves open?
articles.check_answer: A free-form agent can select a dataset and declare it a match with nothing checking the constraints. Typed plans and deterministic operators with a verification step make that check explicit.

articles.title: Groundhog Day for AI agents: Prompt caching patterns for using OpenAI models on Amazon Bedrock
articles.focus: Read up to 'Hello cached world', then jump to the summary list near the end. Skip the long code samples on a first pass.
articles.summary: Models have no memory between requests, so every agent turn resends the tools, instructions, and full history. Prompt caching reuses that processed prefix at a lower input price, and the post walks through implicit and explicit caching across an agent's life.
insights: Caching works only on exactly the same text, so keep tools and instructions serialized the same way and put anything that varies, such as the date or a request ID, after the cached part.
Implicit mode suits a growing conversation, explicit breakpoints suit shared prefixes, and the two can be combined.
A cacheable prefix needs at least 1,024 tokens, and cache writes cost 1.25 times the normal input rate, so measure writes against read savings.
Warm the shared prefix and let that request finish before starting parallel helper agents.
articles.career_fit: Cost and latency are what separate a demo agent from a production one. Being able to explain why prefix order matters is a concrete way to show that in applied AI interviews.
articles.check_question: Why should a timestamp go after the cached instructions and not inside them?
articles.check_answer: Caching needs an identical prefix. A changing timestamp early in the prompt would change the text and stop later requests from reusing the cache.
